## Overview

The Microsoft Dynamics Customer Relationship Management (CRM) IT Service comprises two distinct platforms. The first platform is Microsoft Dynamics CRM Software as a Service (SaaS), which Microsoft manages in their Azure Cloud. The second platform is Azure Platform as a Service (PaaS), which contains components for data migration and integration, including API Management Services (APIM), Azure Data Factory (ADF), Azure Cloud Storage (Azure Blob) and Azure SQL database. Refer to [*U095.1-1 - Service Design Package - CRM - Technical Specifications.docx*](https://mygainwell.sharepoint.com/%3Aw%3A/r/teams/a5b8e89759/Shared%20Documents/Deliverables/Deliverables%20Management/6.%20Service%20Design%20Packages/U095.1-1-Service%20Design%20Package%20-%20CRM%20%28MSDynamics%20and%20Surveys%29%20-%20Technical%20Design%20%26%20Specifications/CRM%20SDP%20Returned%2011.27.2023/U095.1-1%20-%20Service%20Design%20Package%20-%20CRM%20-%20Technical%20Specifications.docx?d=wd2a6bcf4a13d4b6fa383273d4b530a6a&csf=1&web=1&e=eiQSHv)*.*

Azure Active Directory provides Role Based Access Control (RBAC) to these services.

Please refer to the CRM System Admin Training Guide. This added document is intended to provide system administrators with more insight into managing the CRM environment.

### Intelligent Contact Center (ICC) Product Engineering Team

The Gainwell ICC Product Engineering Team has the following responsibilities.

* Single point of contact for Dental BusOps to engage on any issues, questions or concerns associated with the Gabby Platform.
* Provide an entry point in Gainwell MMIS ServiceNow for Incidents, Problem, Change, Service Request Management and Project Intake Requests.
* Host weekly Technical Approval Board (TAB) meetings with account teams.
* Manage the relationship with the Gabby vendor for escalation of incidents and concerns brought forth by the account.

[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP_Appendix_P_Runbook_Example_CRM.md#dental-busops-operations-team-responsibilities]

### Dental BusOps Operations Team Responsibilities

The Dental BusOps Operations Team has the following responsibilities:

* Maintaining a governance panel / delivery manager as a single point of contact for providing ongoing change management oversight.
* Any ServiceNow ticketing requirements within the DHCS Instance of ServiceNow.
* Opening tickets and service requests to engage the ICC Product Engineering team in the Gainwell MMIS Instance of ServiceNow.
* Attending the weekly TAB call.
* Maintaining approved users on the platform.
* Making the appropriate business and technical resources available to the ICC Product Engineering Team to ensure that responses and/or resolution to issues and concerns is achieved.
* Communicating across the Dental BusOps user base.
* Assuming responsibility for network connectivity at remote or host sites.
* Providing ICC Product Engineering Team required access to all systems, information, and documentation to perform Services.
* Communicating to the ICC Product Engineering Team in a timely and regular basis business activity affecting the call center technology.
* Participating in ICC Product Engineering Team collaboration sessions for standard Platform Standards and Processes.
* Providing business continuity plans.

### Process Scope

This section includes activities associated with submitting, categorizing, and routing a request that impacts any aspect of a capability or a client service delivered by the team. Requests are for new capabilities or services or changes to existing capabilities or services.

The scope for Request Management includes:

* Requests related to client production support or implementation activities on the existing capability platform.
* Requests for changes to a standard capability platform and/or supporting processes—also called capability life cycle change requests.
  + These requests include equipment replacements or upgrades, application replacement or upgrades, capacity changes and process changes.
  + These requests are created to support a non-standard client requirement.
  + These requests are routed to the Capability Leader for validation prior to being routed to the Change Control Board for review and action.
* Decisions to direct the request to the ICC Product Engineering team or to other Dental BusOps request handling processes.
* Engagement of project management (if required).
* Monitoring and escalation of a request (if needed).
* Production Environment Projects such as applying an emergency patch which follow the Emergency Change Type process flow associated with the Gainwell Dental BusOps Change Enablement process utilizing the Gainwell MMIS Instance of ServiceNow.

The following items are out of scope for this process section:

* Requests that deal with day-to-day capability and call center operational activities and expenditures as are handled by the Gainwell Dental BusOps account.
* Sales support for Capabilities

Listed here are the key functions/roles associated with the Request Management process described in this section.

* Request Submitter - Depending on the type of request and specific business needs, a request submitter is any of the following roles:
  + Account Support
  + Leveraged Services Team
  + Service Delivery
* Demand Management - Administers the request tool and performs follow up with the submitter to ensure the request is complete, accurate and handled according to its priority.
* Production Support Project Management - Provides project management support to coordinate and manage tasks to fulfill the request.
* Capability Leader - Assigns resources to investigate the request and determines other resources that are needed to evaluate the impact of the request.

### Communication During Incident Management

The following is the method of communication based on priority level for an incident:

* A conference bridge is opened for Priority 1 (P1) and Priority 2 (P2) incidents and Incident Coordination overseen by the Gainwell Network Operations Center (NOC) Team.
* For all P1 incidents, the NOC sends an MIM (Major Incident Management) communication to keep Management up to date. For P2 incidents with immediate risk of P1 impact a MIM is sent, if impact changes to P1 so does the priority level of the MIM.
* For P3 or lower, the communication process is handled directly between account and technician assigned to the incident ticket. The NOC Team is not engaged unless there is high and immediate risk of P1/2.

### Service-Level Determination

Accurate priority level data is critical to support metrics, resource allocation, and the engagement of Problem Management. The priority level of an incident record reflects the actual business impact before service delivery is restored (i.e., during the Incident). Priority level is a measurement of the adverse effect an incident has on a client, environment, or business operation. There are many factors that contribute when assessing the appropriate priority level of an incident, but the following are considered standards:

* Impact – an assessment of the effect the incident is having on the client, environment, or business operation, based on what functionality has been lost or impaired and what level of degradation of service is being experienced because of its loss.
* Urgency – an assessment of how quickly the incident must be resolved. Contractual obligations, the visibility of the event, and the Impact it is causing are all factors that contribute to this assessment.

The combination of these two factors is used to establish the appropriate priority level.

Please refer to the Incident and Problem Management Plan for more details.
page_texts.18:
[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP_Appendix_P_Runbook_Example_CRM.md#adjusting-priority-levels]

### Adjusting Priority Levels

As diagnosis and investigation take place, adjustments to the initial Priority Level may be required to ensure an Incident receives the appropriate level of attention and resource allocation. When the Priority Level must be altered due to an increase or decrease in the Impact and/or Urgency, this section outlines the requirements.

**Raising (upgrading) the priority level** is defined as changing the priority level from one that reflects a lower impact on the client to one that reflects a greater impact (for example, raising the Priority level from 3 to 1).

The Priority level may be raised if the impact to the client is determined to be greater than the current Priority level indicates. This includes Incidents whose Priority level is based on *potential impact* as well as *actual impact*. The Priority level may be raised at any time to reflect an increased Impact or Urgency.

**Lowering (downgrading) the prioritylevel** is defined as changing theprioritylevel from one that reflects a higher impact on the client to one that reflects a lower impact (for example, changing the priority level from 2 to 3).

Because priority level is a measure of the impact experienced by an affected client, environment, or business operation during an incident, the decision to lower the priority level of an incident is carefully considered and properly authorized.
page_texts.19:
[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP_Appendix_P_Runbook_Example_CRM.md#for-priority-level-1-or-2]

#### For Priority Level 1 or 2

The decision to lower the priority level must be agreed to by the client-facing role that directly represents the affected client, environment, or business operation (for Incidents affecting multiple clients, each affected client must have this representation). Examples of this role include:

* Client Delivery Executive
* Client Support Representative
* Production Environment Manager

Each time the Priority level is lowered, the reason for the downgrade and the name of the authorizing party must be documented in the Incident record. Technical support capability groups must obtain and document authorization from this role prior to lowering the Priority of these Incidents. Note: this requirement is waived for Incident records initially opened at a Priority level 1 or 2 for events that upon diagnosis prove not to fit the criteria for these priorities. Examples include false alerts generated by monitoring tools and "single user" issues initially reported as affecting a site. In such cases the downgrade requirement is the same as that for Priority 3 or 4 records.
page_texts.20:
[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP_Appendix_P_Runbook_Example_CRM.md#for-priority-level-3-or-4]

#### For Priority Level 3 or 4

If the priority level is lowered, the reason for the downgrade is documented in the incident record.

For all records, the final priority level must reflect the [actual impact](http://kc.sharepoint.hp.com/sites/kc62/StagingDocsold/Preproduction/Draft%20Severity%20Level%20Standards.htm#Actual_Impact) experienced by the client at the time of the incident.

### Major Incident Process

Only users with the ITIL role in ServiceNow can propose a Major Incident in ServiceNow. If you do not know who is an ITIL user in your account, please reach out to your IT Organization Administrator (ITO ADM).

To propose a Major Incident, the following fields need to be completed or updated:

* Configuration Item:
  + Select Generic-Software
* Symptom:
  + Access / Permissions
  + Connectivity
  + Failure
  + Hardware
  + Inquiry
  + Insufficient Space
  + Slowness / Performance
  + Software
  + Other
* The following fields should already be filled in based on the incident request opened in Service Portal:
  + State of
  + Service
  + Service Offering
  + Short Description
  + Description
* Update the Impact from single user to either of the following:
  + 1 – Enterprise
  + 2 – Site or Dept
* Select “Save”
* Select “Work Notes” and indicate that you have updated the ticket.
* Select the “Hamburger” menu, or right click on the gray bar at the top of the screen and select “Propose Major Incident.”
* You will need add information to the Work Notes describing why this is a P1/P2 outage and how many users are impacted.

1. ![A white background with black lines  Description automatically generated](data:image/png;base64...)Proposing a Major Incident

* Once a Major Incident is proposed, it will show up on the Network Operations Center (NOC) team dashboard and an email will be sent to NOC team members. The user will also need to call the NOC at 877-878-1017. The NOC will ask the user a series of questions (what’s down, when did it start, and who is impacted) and then a Page, a Call, and an Email will be sent out to the assigned group in ServiceNow.
* If the network at your site is down, please contact the NOC at 877-878-1017. The NOC will then Promote/Reject the Major Incident Candidate as required, then the necessary MIM/Incident process will begin.

### ID and CRM License Provisioning

The CRM user’s account is created in the Gainwell California DBO tenant’s Microsoft Entra, when a user is created in DBO tenant, the user must be added to one or more of the existing security groups for the user to be assigned CRM license. Microsoft Entra uses Guest and Member accounts. Most CRM Users are set up as Guests to this CRM tenant, allowing the use of Single Sign On (SSO) credentials to authenticate and authorize access to CRM. Member Accounts are reserved for CRM System Administrators and Developers. These Member Accounts will be assigned a unique User ID and Password with the @californiadbo.onmicrosoft.com domain.

The process for creating a CRM User account starts with creating a ticket within DHCS CA-MMIS SNOW .

The Gainwell SNOW request will provide the required information to set up a new User in CRM Microsoft Entra:

* User First and Last Name
* User Email address

User Location (required that this be United States only)

* Security Group – Role Based – will select one or more from the Service Catalog.
* All the CRM user roles are defined and can be found in *SDP\_CRM\_Appendix\_S\_User\_Roles.xlsx*.

Upon completion of the User setup process:

* The User will receive an Invitation from the System Administrator who set up the User.

Upon accepting the Invitation, the User can navigate to their *My Apps* panel and select the CRM Tile to access the CRM application. A User may access multiple CRM environments, including User Acceptance Testing (UAT), Training, and Production. If so, they will have these three Tiles—one for each environment.

***NOTE****:* *There is a synchronization process between Microsoft Entra and the CRM application. This usually takes a few minutes but could take several hours. Users may see a message saying they are not part of the Organization. If so, ask them to retry in 30 minutes.*

For additional information, refer to the *Access Management Plan*.

## Application Access Error

**Error Code:**

2147812097 Invalid License

**This application requires a license, and you don't have an appropriate license assigned**

![A white background with black text  Description automatically generated](data:image/png;base64...)

Symptoms:

When a user tries to access an app module (business application) that requires an appropriate license and no license is assigned to the user.

Cause:

This issue occurs when an application requires a license, and the administrator hasn't assigned the appropriate license to the user(s) of the application.

Resolution:

The resolution is to create a SNOW ticket request, assign it to APPS-CRM-DENTICAL DBO, and request that the license be assigned. The license name and the application names are present in the error technical details.

![](data:image/png;base64...)

Access to Custom Apps:

For access to custom apps (canvas or model-driven), you need to be assigned a Dynamics 365 Enterprise or Professional license, Power Apps Per User plan or the environment needs to be given Power Apps per app plans (aka app passes). For online information about Power Apps per app plans go to ([About Power Apps per app plans](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/about-powerapps-perapp)).

## Sign in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Error

![](data:image/png;base64...)

![](data:image/png;base64...)

**Error:**

Error messages display when you try to sign into Microsoft Dynamics 365 (online).

**Symptoms:**

When you try to sign into Microsoft Dynamics 365 (online), you receive one of the following errors:

* You are not a member of this organization
* Your account has been disabled
* No instances found for this user ID
* Invalid User Authorization

**Cause:**

This error can occur if a security group is associated with the Dynamics 365 instance, and you aren't a member of that security group.

**Resolution:**

Create a SNOW ticket incident and assign it to APPS-CRM-DENTICAL DBO to ask your Dynamics 365 administrator to add you to a security group associated with the Dynamics 365 instance you are trying to access.

These errors sometimes occur because Microsoft Entra hasn’t finished synchronizing to the CRM Application. Please retry in 30 minutes. Microsoft states that the synchronization can take a few minutes to several hours.

Error:

User will receive a message on their CRM browser session that their session has been logged out due to 15 minutes of inactivity.

User will not be able to access CRM unless they log in again by entering their SSO Credentials.

Cause:

User session was inactive for 15 minutes

**NOTE**: *User will receive a warning two minutes before being logged out for inactivity.*

![A screenshot of a computer  Description automatically generated](data:image/png;base64...)

**Resolution:**

If you have admin privileges you can set the expiration value from 5 minutes to 60 minutes by doing the following changes, however, if you don’t have admin privileges create a SNOW ticket to request change to session timeout:

* On the top right side of the top ribbon bar click on the **Gear Icon** > Select **Advance settings** > **Settings** > **Administration** > **System settings**> Select the **General** tab to open the session parameters page.
* Scroll down to session time out section
* In session time out settings, select **Set Custom**
* In **Duration of inactivity** enter a value between 5 minutes and 60 minutes
* In **how long before the session expires do you want show inactivity warning**, enter the desired value in minutes

The Daily File contains CRM records created or modified the previous day. The End-of-the-Month file contains SLA metrics-based cases and surveys.

Reports will be generated from GIA or ad-hoc reports using the Advanced Filter function in CRM.

### GIA Reports

Three types of reports are sent to GIA:

* Daily Interface Report (Daily) – provides case analytics data from CRM to GIA.
* GIA Metrics Report (Monthly) – provides Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and measures associated with CRM services for providers and members.
* GIA Survey Report (Monthly) provides survey satisfaction results for respondents such as providers, members, or member-authorized representatives.

# Email Encryption Setup

1. Encyption for outbound email is provided via the Proof Point platform of Gainwell.
2. Emails sent from CRM are currently only allowed from a single email account – DBOCustomerService@gainwelltechnologies.com.
3. For the email to be encrypted, the sender needs to insert the word [secure] in brackets into the beginning of the Subject line on the outbound email.
4. If a sender does not add the word ‘secure’ in brackets the email will still be sent however it will not be encrypted.

# Troubleshooting Power Automate Flows

1. Open the Power Automate flow you want to troubleshoot. Under **28-day run history**, it displays all the times the flow ran, including successes and failures.
2. Open the record for the most recently failed flow by clicking on it.

![](data:image/png;base64...)

The error is denoted by a red circle with an exclamation point inside. Additional details about the error associated with the failed run are displayed on the right side of the window.

![](data:image/png;base64...)

1. Click **Edit** from the ribbon to resolve the error.
2. Modify the error and **Resubmit** the changes.

![](data:image/png;base64...)

1. From the ribbon, select **Turn off** to deactivate the Power Automate flow.

![](data:image/png;base64...)
